newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel uproots West Bank trees, arrests Arabs.
newsitem.headline: Israel uproots West Bank trees, arrests Arabs.

text.p: Israeli troops protecting workers uprooting olive trees on Sunday arrested four Palestinians and dispersed others with tear gas near Toura village in the West Bank, Arab witnesses said.
An Israeli official said the trees were planted illegally and only one Palestinian was arrested.
Palestinian sources said the villagers had tried to prevent Israeli authorities from uprooting the 800 trees growing on several hectares (acres) of land.

The sources said Israel destroyed the trees apparently in order to clear a strip on either side of a road travelled frequently by Israeli troops. They said there had been instances of Palestinians stoning Israeli vehicles in the area and then fleeing into the olive groves.

"We were carrying out some activities to remove illegal trees planted on government state-owned land when a crowd appeared this morning. This is an illegal act. There were very minor clashes and I understand that one person was arrested," said Peter Lerner, spokesman for Israel's military authority in the West Bank.
Villagers showed reporters documents issued when Jordan was in control of the area before the 1967 Middle East war which said they owned the land.

Israel handed eight major West Bank towns to Palestinian rule beginning in 1994 under interim peace deals. It still controls rural West Bank areas but has pledged to make further withdrawals of so-far unspecified scope from the rural sector.
